section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the wonder of the eagle in the Chariot, focusing on why the eagle, representing the central line reaching the innermost aspect of Kesser, is more astonishing than the lion on the right.
section.t: And the explanation is,
for it is written,
"Three things are too wondrous for me... the way of the eagle in the sky..."
And it is explained elsewhere
that the wonder is how there can be the face of an eagle, which is an unclean bird, in the supernal Chariot.
And it needs to be understood,
for in the Chariot there is also the face of a lion to the right,
which is an unclean animal,
so why is the wonder specifically about the eagle?
And the explanation of this is,
based on what is explained elsewhere,
that the way of the eagle
(the face of the eagle in the Chariot)
is the matter of the central line.
And this is why he wonders specifically about the face of the eagle,
for the face of the lion is to the right,
for the face of the lion in the Chariot is in the right line, which ascends only in the externality of Kesser,
and this is not so wondrous,
but not so the face of the eagle, which is in the central line, ascending into the innerness of Kesser,
it is exceedingly wondrous how there can be the face of an unclean bird in the innerness of Kesser.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the attribute of mercy, rooted in the innerness of Kesser, falls to the lowest level, called "nesher" from the term for falling, and this is why Israel, who have no connection to the desert, are roused from there like an eagle.
section.t: And the explanation of the matter,
for specifically because the attribute of mercy is rooted in the innerness of Kesser,
therefore it falls to the very lowest level,
and this is why it is called "nesher" (eagle), from the term "neshirah" (falling) and "nefilah" (fall),
for it falls from its level,
even to an unclean bird outside the place of holiness.
And with this the continuation of the verses will be understood,
for it is written before it, "He found him in a desert land,"
for a desert is a place where no man dwells,
meaning it is outside the dwelling of the supernal man,
and likewise outside the dwelling of the Children of Israel, who are called "man"
—"I will liken him to the supernal one"—
for in every Jew there is a holy soul, which is literally a part of G-d above,
and as it is written before this,
"For the portion of Havayah is His people,"
and therefore they have no connection whatsoever to the place of the desert
(which is outside holiness),
and not only does no man dwell
(meaning Israel)
there,
but no man even passed there,
meaning that Israel have no connection to this place.
And this is what continues, "Like an eagle stirring up its nest,"
for to this place the aspect of "nesher" fell.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that even from the lowest place, the ascent is to the highest level, the innerness of Kesser, through the revelation of the eagle aspect, analogous to the soul's descent and return, and the black of the eye representing distance that leads to repentance.
section.t: However, even regarding this place it is said, "He found him in a desert land,"
for even from there "Havayah your G-d will gather you, and from there He will take you."
And the elevation and return from this place is through the revelation of the aspect of "nesher" (eagle) at the very highest level,
the aspect of the innerness of Kesser,
for "from it and within it, the axe is thrown into it,"
and through this they ascend to the innerness of Kesser.
For since whatever is higher descends lower, therefore specifically by ascending from such a distant place,
the ascent is to the highest level.
And this is like what is explained in many places
(from the teachings of the AriZal)
in the explanation of the verse,
"For not by bread alone does man live, but by everything that comes from the mouth of Havayah does man live,"
that the desert needs "that which comes from the mouth of Havayah" in the still, silent, and mineral (domem, tzomeach, chai),
because from the fact that the sparks fell to the very lowest level
(in the still, silent, and mineral below the desert),
it proves that their root is higher,
and therefore specifically through their power they can enliven "that which comes from the mouth of Havayah" in the desert.
And likewise it will be understood below this,
regarding the aspect of "nesher" (eagle), whose matter is the fall outside the place of holiness,
that specifically through the ascent from this place, one ascends to the innerness of Kesser.
And this is the reason for the descent of the soul from a high roof to a deep pit,
from the aspect of "the soul that You placed within me" to "that which You breathed into me"
in this lowly world,
so that in this world there will be an ascent from the very lowest,
specifically in the ladder "planted on the earth,"
specifically,
and through this "its head reaches the heavens,"
to the very highest,
until "the spirit returns to G-d who gave it."
And this is
what continues,
"He formed us as the pupil of His eye,"
for "ishon" (pupil) is the black of the eye, as our sages said,
"A person does not see through the white of the eye, but through the black of the eye,"
for the matter of the black of the eye is the blackness, concealment, distance, etc.
For through contemplating that one is in a place of concealment,
in a distant place,
and "evil and bitter is your forsaking Havayah,"
through this one comes to repentance from the depths of the heart, until intentional sins become for him like merits, and also merits.
